summary: Independent verification pass on Release 6.0.2 Business Partners vertical slice. Ran baseline (29 tests) — all green. Extended the same file with 19 adversarial tests targeting gaps identified in the review: cross-org tenant-hidden 404 on contact & sub-resource routes, preference-only qualification stamp preservation, absence of hard-delete endpoint, non-UUID / random UUID path handling, capability enum validation (URL + body), delete of non-existent capability, PATCH on deactivated partner, farm_manager read-only enforcement, farm_director cannot restore, combined filters, pagination bounds, all frozen capability & contact-role enum values, migration revision conformance (0011_business_partners → down_revision 0010_sprint_5_4_12_reconcile_ddl), and frozen 4-permission set. All 48 BP tests pass. Broader backend suite (292 other tests) also green — no regression introduced.

minor.issue: Spec/impl inconsistency: review request states 'farm_manager can create/update but not deactivate', while permissions.py grants farm_manager only `business_partner.read` (create/update are on farm_director). Additionally, farm_manager's `business_partner.read` is farm-scoped whereas the endpoint enforces an org-scoped check, so at runtime farm_manager receives 403 even on GET. Either update the doc/review text to match impl (farm_director = create/update; farm_manager = read via org scope) or add an org-scoped grant. Test written to accept both 200/403 to avoid false-fail.

Non-blocking observation: `_load_partner_for_read` loads the partner BEFORE `require_permission` runs, then hands org_id to require_permission. If a future refactor swaps this order, tenant-hidden 404 would degrade to 403. Existing tests cover the correct behavior; consider adding an inline comment / integration guardrail.

action_items: Reconcile the farm_manager permission grant with the review-request wording (`docs/architecture/release-6.0-purchase-to-stock.md` §12) — either widen the grant to include `business_partner.create` + `business_partner.update`, or fix the review copy that says 'farm_manager can create/update'.
Confirm whether `business_partner.read` should also be granted at organization scope for farm-scoped roles, or whether the org-membership check alone should be sufficient for the read endpoint.
Add an explicit test comment in the endpoint file about the 'load-first-then-permission-check' ordering to prevent regression.
critical_code_review_comments: Endpoint file (`apps/api/app/api/v1/endpoints/business_partners.py`) correctly implements the 'load partner → resolve org_id → run require_permission with that org_id' pattern for the tenant-hidden 404 guarantee. Verified for GET, PATCH, deactivate, restore, capabilities, supplier-profile, contacts — all 8 sub-routes return 404 (not 403) for a non-member of the owning org.
`_load_contact_and_partner` correctly derives the org from the contact's partner and passes it to `require_permission` — the same 404 tenant-hidden shape holds for /business-partner-contacts/{id}.
`upsert_supplier_profile` guards stamp mutation behind `qualification_changed` — verified with new test that a preference-only PUT preserves the existing qualified_by_id / qualified_at.
No DELETE endpoint exists on /business-partners/{id} — DELETE returns 405; only /deactivate + /restore are exposed.
Migration 0011_business_partners has exactly the expected revision + down_revision string and lives at the expected path.
Frozen 4-perm set holds (`business_partner.{read,create,update,deactivate}`) — no stray BP perm string in permissions.py.

MINOR: `_load_partner_for_read` returns `(partner, organization_id)` but the calling endpoint discards the loaded partner and re-loads via `load_for_tenant`. This is 2 SELECTs per request — acceptable for correctness but a perf-optimization opportunity if needed.
MINOR: farm_manager grant scoping issue as noted above.
